findings.explanation: All three extensions materialize the reified T as T::class.java. getTypeHint<T>() selects Java getTypeHint(Class<?>), which converts the Class to a TypeReference and performs the lookup. The customizer overload passes typeHint::invoke, adapting the same Kotlin callback to Java Consumer<TypeHint.Builder>; the Java Class/Consumer overload forwards it to the TypeReference/Consumer overload, where accept invokes it. The category overload uses *memberCategories, so its elements are spread into Java Class/MemberCategory..., then forwarded to TypeReference/MemberCategory... and applied through TypeHint.builtWith rather than passed as a nested array.

Both Class-based registration overloads first reject a null Class with Assert.notNull, which throws IllegalArgumentException. For a non-null Class whose canonical name is null, both skip forwarding and simply return this. Consequently, the supplied customizer is not invoked for either a rejected null Class or a skipped no-canonical-name Class; member categories likewise are not applied. A valid Class is converted to TypeReference and forwarded.

computeIfAbsent makes repeated registration under the same/equal type key reuse one TypeHint.Builder. Category registration becomes a customizer via TypeHint.builtWith; withMembers adds categories to the builder's HashSet, so registrations accumulate as a set union, duplicate categories collapse, and ordering is unspecified. The builder is installed in the map before accept runs. If a customizer throws, the exception propagates and return this is not reached, but there is no rollback: prior categories and any category additions completed before the throw remain. For a previously absent type, an immediate throw still leaves its new builder registered with an empty category set.

getTypeHint(Class<?>) unconditionally calls TypeReference.of(type), then the TypeReference overload performs a map lookup and builds a hint only when a builder exists. Thus lookup of a valid but unregistered Class returns null without creating state, whereas registration creates the builder and invokes its customizer. TypeReference.of(Class) reaches ReflectionTypeReference.of, which validates both a non-null Class and a non-null canonical name with Assert.notNull. Accordingly, lookup with a no-canonical-name Class throws IllegalArgumentException, while Class-based registration skips it; lookup with null also throws during conversion, while registration has its own explicit null-Class guard.

Each successful lookup builds a new TypeHint, and its constructor takes an immutable copy of the builder's current member-category set. Therefore, a TypeHint returned earlier—and the set returned from its getMemberCategories()—does not change after later registration for the same type. Later registration mutates the retained builder; a fresh lookup observes a new snapshot containing the accumulated categories.
